name: Aloysia

project_scope.source: Live Master Plant Pool checked 2026-10-12; two distinct source-pool entries; genus absent from Genus Study Index at selection
project_scope.learner_admission: Both approved by source-pool membership; range status is independent; A. virgata is an introduced/cultivated encounter comparison, not a target-zone-native certification
project_scope.mode: Genus lesson only; no species installation or range adjudication

shared_genus_recognition: Woody, often aromatic shrubs with opposite simple leaves, no interpetiolar stipules and small tubular, usually four-lobed flowers in raceme-like clusters.
In the local source-pool pair, flowers are white and fragrant; color and scent alone do not separate species.
Verbenaceae family confirmation requires inflorescence and ovary/fruit architecture, not square stems or aroma.
look_here_first: START WITH A MATURE LEAF + AN INTACT FLOWERING RACEME: measure multiple fully expanded leaves and photograph an axillary raceme side-on. A. gratissima generally has much smaller leaves and tightly crowded flowers in short dense racemes; A. virgata has larger, usually toothed leaves and loose, often zigzag racemes with visibly separated flower bases. Confirm using several shoots; do not rely on odor or flower color.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Usually 10–20 × 5–8 mm in Kew treatment; regional north-central Texas flora reports 3–27 × 2–8 mm.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Measure 5–10 fully expanded leaves on multiple mature shoots; exclude tiny axillary fascicle leaves.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Usually entire, but some forms/juvenile shoots show teeth.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Usually distinctly dentate; depth varies and some intermediates occur.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Backlit close-up of mature leaf edge with ruler; do not key by teeth alone.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Often oblong to oblanceolate with obtuse or rounded apex.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Often ovate to elliptic with acute tip, sometimes narrower.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Matched mature blade scans; note variability.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Often paler than upper face, but not densely white-tomentose.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Green on both sides, often paler below; underside hairs variable.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Matched abaxial macro; this is supporting, not an exclusive discriminator.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Dense axillary raceme; flower bases crowded.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Lax, often flexuose axillary raceme; individual flower bases readily visible.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Side-on flowering raceme with scale and arrows to adjacent flower bases.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Often solitary dense raceme in each axil; typically 2–3 cm long (occasionally 5 cm) in Kew treatment.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Often several lax racemes from a leaf axil; flowering axes may zigzag.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Whole axil photo showing point of origin and all racemes; do not assume raceme count is invariant.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Small leafy fascicles often conspicuous in axils in regional Texas descriptions.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: No comparable diagnostic fascicle emphasis in cited Kew treatment; assess as secondary character only.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Macro of nonflowering node with young leaves and mature leaves together.

species_comparison_matrix.gratissima: Often strongly branched, small shrub; some branchlets spinescent.
species_comparison_matrix.virgata: Usually larger vigorous shrub with elongated branches; growth form varies with pruning/frost.
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Whole-plant image plus young branchlet close-up; habit only supports leaf/raceme evidence.
Do not use to split species.

field_decision_sequence: 1. Confirm opposite leaves and axillary small-flowered racemes; keep other Verbenaceae open until the flower and fruit fit.
2. On several mature shoots measure fully expanded leaves (not young axillary clusters): consistently small ~1–2 cm blades suggest A. gratissima; ~4–9 cm blades suggest A. virgata.
3. Photograph intact racemes side-on: densely packed short racemes support A. gratissima; lax, flexuose racemes with exposed flower bases support A. virgata.
4. Check mature margin, apex and axillary leafy fascicles as secondary confirmation; do not use tooth presence alone.
5. If leaf sizes intermediate or dense/lax inflorescence evidence conflicts, leave Aloysia sp. and hand off specimen/photographs for review rather than forcing a species.
overlap_cautions: A. gratissima has geographically variable leaf size and occasional serrate forms, including forms formerly distinguished at varietal rank; toothed leaves do not automatically imply A. virgata.

Kew's Aloysia gratissima treatment reports specimens difficult to separate from A. virgata and possible introgression outside the local region; do not infer that a Texas plant is a hybrid without voucher-level evidence.
The raceme comparison works best on fully flowering intact inflorescences; young or weathered racemes can look falsely sparse.
Frost damage and horticultural pruning can alter A. virgata habit and leaf size; never use shrub height alone.
Both have small white fragrant flowers. Odor, flower color and insect visitation are not species separators.
Source-pool inclusion does not certify target-zone nativity. Preserve A. gratissima and A. virgata range labels separately from learner admission.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confusable: Opposite leaves and small tubular flowers in elongated spikes.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Herbaceous erect Verbena spike architecture versus woody Aloysia with axillary racemes; confirm mature fruit and floral insertion.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confusable: Woody opposite-leaved Verbenaceae with fragrant foliage and clustered small flowers.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Lantana has dense rounded flower heads and fleshy drupe-like fruits, not Aloysia's elongated racemes and small dry fruits.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.why_confusable: Woody opposite leaves and small clustered flowers; can be confused before fruiting.
local_source_pool_lookalikes.separate: Large serrate leaves and compact axillary cymes followed by purple drupes; family Lamiaceae, not Aloysia.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched five-leaf sets per species on mm grid; arrows at length/width endpoints; exclude young axillary fascicles.
Matched side-on intact flowering axillary racemes at same scale; arrows to crowded vs exposed flower bases.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.role: raceme axis flexuosity and axil origin
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Full flowering node with branching and entire racemes visible; arrows marking solitary dense vs multiple lax flexuose axes.
Matched close-ups of mature blades with edge and tip labels; include toothed A. gratissima exception if documented.
10× matched underside macros; label hairs and avoid treating them as sole discriminator.
Matched vegetative-node macros with young leafy shoots and main leaf pair labeled.
Whole shrub and branchlet; show spinescent tips where present, with caution on frost/pruning.
Compare axillary raceme, terminal spike, capitate flower head and Callicarpa axillary cyme; label inflorescence insertion and fruit.

existing_media_reuse.note: Family module has useful Verbenaceae/Lamiaceae/Rubiaceae comparisons and existing Lantana licensed references. No exact Aloysia user/Joey file or rights-verified image was confirmed this run; do not fabricate image paths or licenses.

handoffs.task: Acquire licensed exact-species leaf-size and dense-vs-lax raceme matched photos first, then other checklist roles. Preserve image provenance and verify annotation arrows.
Both Aloysia source-pool species absent from canonical manifest on 2026-10-12. Install only after identity gate; keep source-pool admission separate from native-range status.

If a specimen has intermediate blade size/teeth or contradictory raceme packing, compare Kew treatments and voucher-level material for A. gratissima / A. virgata; do not assert hybrids from appearance alone or reopen settled range decisions.
